# By handler

What handles each entry of the catalog, and what that handler is.

[All topics](README.md) · [Roadmap](roadmap.md)

<a id="stub-generator"></a>
## the stubs

The bpy stubs (`.pyi` files) any Python type checker or editor reads: Blender's own (builtin, 5.2 and later) or
fake-bpy-module. A convention the stubs can state as plain Python typing needs nothing else.

No entry yet.

<a id="runtime-probe"></a>
## the runtime probe

Facts read from a running Blender and written into the stubs: what its startup scripts register, the Value types of
properties defined in C, the members a context really has.

No entry yet.

<a id="source-parser"></a>
## the Blender source parser

Facts read from Blender's C and Python source that no running Blender reports: which pointers are never `None`, which
enum values a function accepts.

No entry yet.

<a id="typechecker"></a>
## the add-on typechecker

ty-blender, a fork of ty that reads an add-on as Blender loads it: property annotations, what `register()` adds,
operator idnames, the members a poll guarantees. It reports what Blender would reject as `blender-*` diagnostics.

- [A legacy single-file add-on](addons.md#legacy-scene-counter) (handled): A module with a `bl_info` dict is a legacy add-on.
- [The add-on's own preferences](addons.md#own-preferences) (handled): `preferences.addons[__package__].preferences` is the add-on's own `AddonPreferences` subclass when the key names the add-on, not the stub's `AddonPreferences | None`.
- [A property declared as an annotation](properties.md#annotated-property) (handled): A Property host declares its properties as class annotations, `name: IntProperty(...)`.

<a id="runtime-typechecker"></a>
## the runtime add-on typechecker

The add-on typechecker run inside Blender, against the add-on as it is registered: for what only exists once the
add-on runs.

No entry yet.

<a id="blender-fix"></a>
## a fix in Blender

A change to Blender itself (its stubs, its API or its docs) that makes the convention checkable by any tool.

No entry yet.

<a id="linter-profile"></a>
## the linter profile

The ruff configuration for add-on code (`config/ruff/`): rules that misfire on Blender conventions are turned off or
narrowed, and rules that catch Blender mistakes are turned on.

No entry yet.

<a id="blender-runtime"></a>
## Blender at runtime

Blender itself, when the add-on runs: it raises, prints a warning or rejects the class. The entry says what it does
and shows the evidence.

No entry yet.

## Nothing

Entries nothing handles yet, or not classified yet.
